purpose: Distinguish memory candidates, selected working memory, memory actually passed into the cognitive pipeline, and the source selected as the reply memory anchor.

stages.retrieved_candidates: All nonempty candidates returned by memory channels, including rows later deduplicated.
stages.candidate_pool: Unique memory candidates that entered salience ranking after deduplication.
stages.selected_working_memory_trace_ids: Top-k candidate identifiers selected by the unchanged working-memory ranking.
stages.passed_to_leftbrain: Identified memory records that were serialized into a memory_data channel visible to LeftBrain.
stages.memory_anchor_trace_id: The passed memory record selected as the explicit reply anchor.
stages.causally_supported: Reserved for a later paired intervention where removing or replacing this exact trace_id changes a preregistered downstream outcome.

interpretation_limits: Candidate presence does not prove model use.
Passing a record to LeftBrain does not prove causal influence.
Selecting a memory anchor is a system decision and is not evidence of a human using the same memory.
Causal language is forbidden until an exact trace_id intervention passes its preregistered gate.
behavior_invariants: No prompt, reply policy, memory write, or runtime activation changes.
Stored records retain their database memory_id; transient records receive a deterministic derived trace_id.
next_authorized_experiment: A frozen paired intervention that removes or replaces one passed trace_id while keeping every other input fixed.
